title: Git LFS repository configuration can execute local commands during object transfers
summary: Git LFS can run attacker-selected commands when fetching objects from a malicious repository. One flaw misparses line-ending characters in submodule configuration; another allows repository .lfsconfig keys to select custom transfer commands.

severity.rationale: Repository content can trigger local code execution during normal LFS object fetching. Agents and CI routinely process untrusted repositories without a person inspecting each configuration value.

affected.note: CVE-2026-105802 affects versions since 0.6.0. CVE-2026-105803 affects versions since 1.3.0. Both are fixed in 3.8.1.

exposure: Fetching LFS objects from attacker-controlled repositories exposes local processes. The submodule flaw requires initialized submodules; the .lfsconfig flaw does not require them.

remediation.details: Install 3.8.1 or later. Until then, avoid untrusted repositories or disable Git LFS. Disabling submodule initialization addresses only the submodule flaw.
remediation.risk: Medium. Disabling LFS or submodules interrupts dependent checkouts.

verification: Confirm git-lfs reports 3.8.1 or later in each checkout worker; test an ordinary trusted LFS fetch.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record from directly inspected primary sources; independent review pending.
